  • and practised from childhood - the poem exposes how the school reproduces caste inequalities

  • social injustices and human suffering in the world - challenge the listener to think about
  • issues like war, freedom, and empathy - phrase "The answer is blowin' in the wind" suggests
  • that solutions to these problems are evident but often ignored or unacknowledged - poem
  • critiques apathy and encourages awareness and action.

questions.question: How does Paul Theroux describe his fellow passengers in Chapter 2? What do these observations reveal about his style of travel writing?

  • appearance and mannerisms- Duffill appears frail, shabby and mysterious, while Molesworth is
  • portrayed as a witty, wine-loving actor's agent with a military bearing - he also notices the
  • unusually tall Belgian girl, the suspicious French mother, the anxious American couple and other
  • eccentric travellers - these detailed, humorous and ironic observations reveal his travel writing as
  • keenly observant, character-centered and rich in social satire. ()

questions.question: Describe the mock military exercise arranged by Gulliver and explain how it reflects his efforts to gain the Emperor’s trust.
questions.solution_html:
• The Lilliputian cavalry and infantry performed military drills and formations between them.
  • Gulliver stood with his legs apart while the Lilliputian cavalry and infantry marched safely
  • between them as part of a mock military exercise - he remained perfectly still and followed the
  • Emperor's instructions with great care - the display demonstrated his obedience, self-control and
  • harmless intentions - by cooperating fully with the Emperor, Gulliver strengthened the Emperor's
  • confidence in him and earned greater trust and favour. ()
